prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor living room with a man standing in the foreground about 1.2 to 1.5 metres in front of and slightly to the left of the camera wearer, while a couch, side tables with lamps, and a recessed wall recess behind him at roughly 3 to 4.5 metres distance (separated from him by about 2 to 3 metres). In frames 1 and 2, the man's head is pitched downward toward a handheld smartphone held within his own arm's reach at waist level, and a foreground surface or object at the bottom-left sits within arm's reach (under 1 metre) of both the camera wearer and the man. Across frames 3 to 5, the man raises his head, straightens his posture, steps slightly closer (brightening his torso and right arm to roughly 1.0 to 1.2 metres away), and turns his head and gaze from facing the camera wearer in frame 3 to looking toward the right of the frame in frames 4 and 5, while his lower body remains cropped below the bottom edge. The depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the floor, the recess of the left wall alcove, and the man's subtle forward torso approach across frames 3 to 5 much clearer than the RGB image alone. However, the map is unreliable around small thin objects and high-contrast edges, merging the man's hands, lanyard badge, and phone into his torso in frames 3 to 5 and flattening the glass coffee table and dark couch cushions into the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground man ('person' at ~1.0 to 1.5 metres in front of the camera wearer) and the background sofa ('couch' at ~3.5 metres behind him and to his right), clearly showing how the man's torso occludes the middle section of the couch and splits its visible mask into two separate left and right regions. In frames 1 and 2, as the man faces forward and looks down at the phone in his hands (within his arm's reach at ~1.2 metres from the camera), the map segments the handheld device near the bottom of his torso, before he lowers the phone out of view and turns his head from facing the camera wearer (frame 3) to looking right (frames 4 and 5). As the man steps slightly forward and shifts left-of-center from frame 3 to frame 5, the occluded gap between the left and right couch segments shifts accordingly and more of the right couch section becomes visible. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation map explicitly delineates the exact pixel boundaries where the man's silhouette occludes the furniture behind him and highlights small foreground items near the lower edge. However, the map is unreliable in object classification and completeness: it mislabels the man's phone as a 'toothbrush' in frame 1 and a 'remote' in frame 2, hallucinates 'remote' masks on his lanyard badge (frame 5) and on coffee table items to his right (frames 3 to 5), mislabels the left armchair/table area as part of the 'couch', and completely misses the walls, lamps, side tables, and coffee table.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the man standing 1.0 to 1.5 metres in front of the camera wearer, with yellow torso, arm, and facial landmarks above and magenta hand keypoints below at waist level, while omitting all background furniture and objects. In frames 1 and 2, the compressed vertical distance between the facial landmarks and the shoulder line captures his head tilted down toward his hands, which are brought together within his arm's reach in front of his abdomen (with his right hand rendered in magenta and his left wrist near it). By frame 3, his head keypoints rise well above the shoulder line and sit symmetrically as he faces and looks directly toward the camera wearer while his arms drop toward the bottom edge of the frame (partly cropped out of view). In frames 4 and 5, the facial keypoints shift asymmetrically toward the right of his head axis, capturing his head turning to look to the right while his right elbow bends to bring his magenta right hand back up near his lower chest/stomach. The pose map makes the kinematic trajectory of his head pitch/yaw, shoulder orientation, and right-hand articulation across the five frames immediately apparent without visual clutter from his patterned jersey, though it is unreliable where the lower body and left hand fall near or below the frame boundary—dropping the left-hand magenta skeleton entirely, missing the lower left arm in frames 4 and 5, and producing tangled limb connections in frame 2.
